title: Family child-care homes: totals only
question: How many licensed family child-care homes are there, where, how many does the City fund, and what public money can be tied to them?
finding: The State counted 884 licensed family child-care homes with 8,504 places in San Francisco on 29 June 2023. Its current file lists only large homes: 292 open with 4,028 places, against 278 at the start of 2022. The City's network of funded programmes lists 372 homes (June 2025), more than twice its 177 centres; they cluster in ZIP codes 94112, 94134, 94124. Money that can be tied to homes as a group: federal meal payments of $3.7 million for 2,251 children fed on an average day in 2024-25, and $2.1 million of State contracts for home networks in 2025-26. Voucher and City money paid to homes cannot be separated from money paid to centres at any level: it is inside the referral agencies' unnamed onward payments.
how: Large-home counts and places by ZIP code are from the State licensing file of 8 November 2026 (which lists homes licensed for 12 or 14 children only); the 2022 figure is rebuilt from first-licensed and closed dates in the same file. Homes in the City network are a count by ZIP code of the Department of Early Childhood's list of funded family child-care providers; the list itself is not kept. Eligible and subsidised children by ZIP code are from the Controller's 2019 audit and describe June 2018, all kinds of care. Any count under five is left blank and ZIP codes with fewer than five homes on both lists are added into one row.
limits: Family child-care homes are private residences: none is listed, located or described here. The State's current file leaves out small homes, which are most homes, so the ZIP figures understate supply; the City list includes small homes, so the two columns do not count the same thing and a ZIP can show more funded homes than large homes. The 2019 layer of the licensing data double-counts homes and was not used, so there is no reliable count by year before 2022. No public source gives voucher dollars, funded places or enrolled children by ZIP code or by kind of provider; the referral agencies' payment ledgers and the City's monthly enrolment reports would.
